before: A separate stopping construction requires many similar small gains and stopping at the earliest qualifying iteration; adding initial iterations exempt from stopping changes it.
after: A separate synthetic stopping construction shows that a small change between consecutive selected QSCI energies need not bound the remaining total energy error: many similar small-gain modes can remain omitted. Its literal rule stops at the earliest iteration whose consecutive energy change is below a prescribed consecutive-energy tolerance, with no minimum iteration count. Mandatory initial iterations exempt from that test postpone the stopping point in this construction, so its first-update conclusion assumes no such exemption; the exemption does not make energy increments alone a general error bound.
